text:
Maya Nguyen: Quick check — we're still leaning gRPC-internal + REST-external for the new generate endpoint, right? Thinking about streaming behavior and SDK ergonomics.
Jonah Patel: that's the current proposal, yes. gRPC for service-to-service gives us bidi/stream options. REST in front for 3rd-party clients and browser fallbacks.
Sara Kim: two operational-ish concerns: 1) quota enforcement — do we enforce at the gateway or at the model service? 2) telemetry traces — need consistent request ids across the proxy boundary.
Liam O'Connor: for quotas I'd prefer gateway-level enforcement for predictable rate shaping. But we should emit a signed header so downstream services can trust the gateway decision, not re-check.
Maya Nguyen: signed header + upstream trust makes sense. But what about bursty traffic and batching — gateway may want to batch into a single gRPC stream to backend, which complicates per-token billing attribution.
Jonah Patel: agreed. Two options: a) gateway keeps token accounting per-subrequest and forwards accounting metadata with each chunk; b) move billing to the model service and have it emit per-request token deltas back to gateway async. Both have tradeoffs.
Sara Kim: option (a) keeps billing deterministic at the gateway but increases metadata traffic. Option (b) centralizes billing but coupling increases. Also consider partial failures: if gateway says "accepted" then fails to persist billing, we need reconciliation.
Product Ops: From console/UX POV, we want token-level breakdowns surfaced per route and per rollout. If billing shifts to service, console needs new telemetry ingest points.
Maya Nguyen: on the streaming contract — backend will expose: ```rpc Generate(GenerateRequest) returns (stream TokenChunk);``` where TokenChunk includes chunk_payload + provenance headers. Gateway will translate to chunked HTTP/2 or SSE for clients. Thoughts?
Jonah Patel: the proto stream is fine. Important: include per-chunk sequence IDs and original request id so tracing + reassembly is deterministic.
Liam O'Connor: also add a compact token_count field to each TokenChunk so we can attribute cost without re-tokenizing. Critical for accuracy.
Sara Kim: telemetry correlation: recommend X-Rd-Req-Id, X-Rd-Signature, and a routed-service header chain. Logs should include both gateway and service spans with the same root. We can enforce presence in an internal linter.
Maya Nguyen: rollout plan idea: start with direct gRPC between gateway and a canary model service behind a feature flag. Gateway behavior switch: streaming passthrough vs full fanout/batch mode. Gradual traffic % and metric checks (latency, error-rate, token-accounting-delta).
Jonah Patel: +1. Add a canary signal for "token-accounting-delta" < 0.5% before increasing traffic. Also check console dashboards for missing spans.
Product Ops: will add dashboard tiles for token-accounting-delta, per-route latency p50/p95, and chunk-reordering errors. Need an event when the canary flips so customers with dedicated infra see the change.
infra-bot: deploy started: gateway-canary v0.8.1 -> infra-canary cluster (job id: 6823).
Sara Kim: minor perf note — streaming over HTTP/1.1 SSE in browsers will force a different translation path; keep an eye on Nagle/TCP small writes. Might want a small coalescing buffer in gateway for SSE clients.
Liam O'Connor: agree. Coalesce up to ~20ms or 512 bytes for SSE. For internal gRPC no coalesce.
Maya Nguyen: OK — action items: 1) add token_count to TokenChunk proto (Sara + Jonah), 2) gateway to sign header + sequence ids (Jonah), 3) infra to add coalesce for SSE paths (Liam), 4) Product Ops to add tiles and canary event (Product Ops). I'll open the RFC PR with these decisions and a rollout checklist. :thumbsup:
Jonah Patel: thanks — I'll prototype the token_count + sequence ids this week.
Maya Nguyen: thanks all.
